cards.text: Every tribe in Israel has its land now, except the Levites. Their share isn't a chunk of land. Their share is the priesthood of the LORD (Joshua 18:7). So at Shiloh, the Levite family heads walk up to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, Israel's leader, and the heads of the other tribes, and they bring up a command the LORD gave.

cards.question: The Levite leaders say the LORD gave a command about them. Who did the LORD give that command through?
The Levites have no land of their own. What does the LORD's command say they should be given?
Along with the cities, the Levites ask for pasturelands for their ___.

cards.text: Now picture it. These tribes JUST got their land, and here come the Levites asking for cities. I shared a junk drawer with dead batteries who argued for YEARS over which one had more charge left, so friend, I'm bracing myself.

cards.question: So how do the tribes of Israel answer the Levites' request for cities?

answers.text: They give cities out of their own land
They tell the Levites to wait a year
They point them to land not yet conquered

cards.question: The Israelites give the Levites these cities by the command of the LORD.

cards.text: That's a LOT of city names, friend, so I'll spare you the roll call. The cities are handed out by lot, clan by clan, from all the other tribes: first Aaron's descendants, the priests, then the rest of Kohath's clans, then Gershon's, then Merari's. The priests get Hebron, though its fields and villages had already gone to Caleb son of Jephunneh, and cities of refuge like Hebron and Shechem are on the list too. Forty-eight cities in all, and every one of them has its own pasturelands (Joshua 21:41-42).

Now the writer steps back from all those city names to look at the whole picture, like me stepping back to admire a counter full of sealed cookie boxes. And it starts with the land the LORD swore to give Israel's fathers.

cards.question: How much of the land He swore to Israel's fathers does the LORD give Israel?
Once the LORD gives Israel the land, they take possession of it and settle in it.
Just as He swore to their fathers, the LORD gives Israel ___ on every side.

cards.text: Rest. On EVERY side. After all those years of marching and battles, that's like the alarm clock finally going quiet for good.

cards.question: None of Israel's enemies can stand against them. Why not?

answers.text: The LORD handed them all over to Israel
Israel's army had grown too big to beat
Every enemy signed a peace treaty

cards.text: The chapter ends with one more line, about all the good promises the LORD made to the house of Israel.

cards.question: A few of the LORD's good promises to the house of Israel had failed.

cards.text: Not ONE failed. Everything was fulfilled. Friend, I once promised a baker a batch by noon and pulled it out at a quarter after, and I'm STILL hearing about it. The LORD's record? Perfect.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: "Every tribe in Israel has its land now, except the Levites." / "Their share isn't a chunk of land." / "Their share is the priesthood of the LORD (Joshua 18:7)." / "So at Shiloh..."

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: "Every tribe in Israel has its land now" is a Bible fact from outside the passage (the land division finished in Joshua 19:51), but it has no reference. The Joshua 18:7 fact on the same card does have one.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Farmland in every tribe" is close to the right content. The Levites are given pasturelands with their cities, from all the tribes (21:2-3, 41-42), so a baker could argue it is right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing from the passage. It is only a joke between cards 4 and 6, yet it cites Joshua 21:2 without using anything from that verse.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The joke compares two different actions. The tribes are being asked to give up cities, but the batteries are arguing over which one has the most charge left. The comparison does not share the core action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card only repeats the answer from card 12 ("Rest. On EVERY side.") and adds a joke. It does not move the passage forward. It also adds "all those years of marching and battles" from outside the passage without a reference.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.
